## The search

A node is a simulated state, identified by its formation, the disk's
connected region and the box's pose within a certified radius
([Node identity](node-identity.qmd)). From a node, the candidates are
the edits that pass [the hold gate](hold-gate.qmd); each expansion calls the
[local solver](local-solver.qmd) Λ, which is the expensive part. The search
is policy-guided (Levin tree search, or policy-guided heuristic search): a
ranker gives a probability π to each candidate edit, nodes are expanded in
order of depth divided by the probability of their path, Λ is charged when
a node is expanded, and edits the gate rejects get π = 0. For this order,
Orseau and Lelis bound the number of expansions by depth / probability of
the solution. The theory note extends the bound to duplicate states (with the
safe duplicate rule and the node key of [Node identity](node-identity.qmd))
and to a Λ that fails at random (with restarts).

## The ranker

- **Inputs:** one token per contact template (type, gap, normal,
  contact-set length, whether it is on), one per body, and one for the goal;
  attention across tokens, with learned biases for pairs that are related by
  containment or share a body or an environment element.
- **Output:** a score per candidate edit, normalized over the candidates into
  π.
- **Training:** supervised, from searches that call Λ without guidance on
  many scene instances: the policy-guided-search loss on solution paths, plus
  a cross-entropy on whether each Λ call succeeded.
- **Baselines:** search without guidance; the gate's margin as the score; and
  a learned feasibility classifier with uniform-cost search on −Σ ln P
  (Hauser, Bretl and Latombe, ICRA 2005).

## Scene families

| Family | Scene and goal |
|---|---|
| F1. Step, randomized | step height, box size, friction, starts; goals on the platform; also lowering the box from the platform |
| F2. Staircase | two or three steps of random rise and tread |
| F3. Wall and ledge | topple the box against a wall, or lift it onto a ledge beside it |

Each family with one or two disks, and the motor limit as a parameter (two
weak disks still need the environment; two strong ones can lift the box).
Validity is computed from the geometry for each family
([Issues](issues.qmd#validity)).

**Teacher search: the first full run (Nov 8–9).** The pipeline generates
seeded step instances, runs the search with a teacher ranker, and logs every Λ
call with the gate's verdicts as training data for the ranker. Its first small
check solved none; the transfers it failed were real realizer failures (makes
that never reached the contact, disk transfers planned as a retreat, contacts
placed at feature ends, hand-overs lingering in a tie), and the fixed realizer
accepts 51 of the 76 it had failed. The full run (200 instances; the relaxed
gate, the learned break skill, retries from other nodes of a key):

| Task | Solved | Λ calls per solve |
|---|---|---|
| Disk contact on the box's side (sub-goal) | 40/40 | 5.1 |
| Box flush on the riser (sub-goal) | 40/40 | 17.5 |
| The pivot formation (sub-goal) | 39/40 | 18.8 |
| Lift onto the platform | 0/40 | — |
| Lower to the floor | 0/40 | — |

7,795 Λ calls (4,954 accepted) are recorded as training data
(`cmg/scripts/step4/teacher/results/t-full/merged/`). Lifting has since been
solved in 5 of 10 instances with a second learned skill
([the local solver](local-solver.qmd#learned-skill)). Lowering is open: the
only edit off the platform, onto the step corner, is a balance Λ<sub>qs</sub>
can't hold (0/52), and nothing brings the box to the edge.

**Baseline: the contact-mode-guided planner (CMGMP).** Built from the authors'
code without root (in a container on Juno) and patched for the disk's 1 N
limit. Its plan for lowering, executed in our simulator and graded by the same
strict test, **succeeds**: the box comes off the platform and rests flat on
the floor.

**Evaluated on 50 shared test starts** (25 per task; 60 s per start on one
CPU core, with restarts; settings chosen on 10 separate tuning starts; every
plan executed in our MJX simulator and graded by the same strict test):

| Task | Plan returned | Strict success | 95% CI | Median time to success |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lift | 11/25 | **6/25** | 11–43% | 45.2 s |
| Lower | 25/25 | **19/25** | 57–89% | 39.4 s |

Lift plans are rare, and half of them fail in execution because the box doesn't
hold the goal; lower plans come easily, but 50 of 71 executions don't hold the
goal, and retries within the budget give 19/25.

**Not yet a paired comparison.** Our planner lifts 5/10 with the learned
skills (7/10 with the proposed tie rule) and lowers none, but on different
instances and with a budget counted in Λ calls; a script pairs the two once our
planner runs on the same 50 starts. So far the baseline is ahead on lowering,
ours on lifting.

*Caveats:* the baseline plans quasi-statically with a point finger, while
execution is dynamic with soft contacts; moves between its planned contacts are
tracked along straight lines without collision planning, so some execution
failures may be the executor's; its 1 N limit is applied per contact component
(up to about 1.4 N along a world axis); and its contact-mode code was patched for
the box wedged into the floor–riser corner.

**Built (Nov 8): the validity tables for all three families.** The builder
now takes any polygonal environment and a rectangular box. It reproduces the
step's tables exactly, and built the two new families (default dimensions;
random-instance ranges are documented, not yet sampled):

| | Step | F2 staircase (2 steps) | F3 wall and ledge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certified valid formations | 357 | 649 | 473 |
| Nodes of W (recognizable, vertex–vertex only alone) | 328 | 592 | 443 |
| Excluded sets | 560 pairs + 1 triple | 1,624 pairs + 5 triples | 840 pairs + 10 triples |
| Compound edges (local rule, ρ = 25 mm) | 92 | 172 | 144 |

New in the families: concave corners the box can wedge into (80 staircase
formations, 42 wall-and-ledge), and pivot-like compound edges at every convex
corner. Neither has collinear edges, so the "pit" case of the theory note
doesn't arise yet.

**The test:** a 2 × 2 table of transfer, holding out an environment family
(F3) and holding out the number of disks, with cost measured in Λ calls. A
targeted literature search found learned guidance for contact or mode search
tested on held-out instances, objects, object counts or robot counts, but
not on a held-out family of environments; the closest work counts solver
calls with learned feasibility for pick-and-place (Ortiz-Haro et al., ICRA
2023).
